qa_pairs.question: Seven years after the initial framework for duty exemptions on specific machinery was established on June 10, 2010, the government issued a new SRO on June 1, 2017, targeting local computer manufacturing. What is the number of this 2017 SRO, and what is the threshold rate above which import duties are exempted?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven years later, on June 1, 2017, the government issued S.R.O. No. 131-AIN/2017/17/Customs. Under this instrument, for local computer manufacturing, an exemption is granted on the import of specified goods from import duties that exceed 1% (one percent) ad valorem, alongside a full exemption of regulatory duties, value-added tax, and supplementary duties (if any).

qa_pairs.question: Five years after S.R.O. No. 157-AIN/2011/2343/Customs was issued on June 9, 2011, the government published a new SRO on June 2, 2016, which amended a previous 2013 notification (S.R.O. No. 150-AIN/2013/2437/Customs). What is the number of this 2016 SRO, and what specific H.S. Code substitution does it make for Heading 85.37?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, on June 2, 2016, the government issued S.R.O. No. 171-AIN/2016/33/Customs. This order amended S.R.O. No. 150-AIN/2013/2437/Customs by replacing the H.S. Code '8537.10.90' with '8537.10.99' under Heading 85.37.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after S.R.O. No. 147-AIN/2013/2434/Customs was issued on June 6, 2013, the government issued another SRO on June 4, 2015, which amended S.R.O. No. 343-AIN/2013/2466/Customs. What is the number of this 2015 SRO, and what is the H.S. Code and description of the goods listed under Heading 28.40 in its substituted Table?
qa_pairs.answer: Two years later, on June 4, 2015, the government issued S.R.O. No. 155-AIN/2015/35/Customs. Its substituted Table lists H.S. Code '2840.20.10' with the description 'Disodium octaborate tetrahydrate' under Heading 28.40.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the government issued S.R.O. No. 219-AIN/2017/57/Customs on July 1, 2017, they amended it with a new SRO on June 7, 2018. What is the number of this 2018 SRO, and what is the Regulatory Duty (RD) rate specified in its substituted TABLE-II for 'Starches' under Heading 11.08?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on June 7, 2018, the government issued S.R.O. No. 159-AIN/2018/25/Customs. In its substituted TABLE-II, the Regulatory Duty (RD) rate for 'Starches' under Heading 11.08 (excluding 1108.20.00) is set at 10%.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the rules for Green Channel usage were established; what change was introduced to Green Channel procedures one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2011-06-09, the rules were updated to authorize customs officers to perform random scanning and examination of up to 5% of passengers passing through the Green Channel.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the baggage rules in effect as of 2011-06-09, what specific restriction on jewelry imports was introduced three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2014-06-05, specific weight limits were introduced, allowing passengers to import duty-free up to 100 grams of gold jewelry or 200 grams of silver jewelry, provided no single type of ornament exceeds 12 pieces.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2014-06-05 regulations on jewelry, what major update to personal baggage weight allowances occurred two years later in 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-04-08, regulations were updated to specify that passengers aged twelve and older arriving by air or water could import up to 65 kilograms of personal hand, cabin, and checked baggage duty-free.

qa_pairs.question: Eight years later, how did the security procedures for containerized transit shift from the manual sealing practices established in 2010?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2018, the Electronic Seal and Lock Service Rules were introduced, mandating the use of electronic seal and lock services for containerized transit, replacing manual sealing methods with automated security measures.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial PSI exemption list established in 2010-06-10, what change occurred one year later regarding the exemption list?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2011-06-09, SRO 158/2011 was issued to formally update the list of goods exempted from mandatory pre-shipment inspection requirements.

qa_pairs.question: Following the issuance of SRO 178/2012 on 2012-06-07, what specific regulatory update took place twenty days later?
qa_pairs.answer: Twenty days later, on 2012-06-27, SRO 235/2012 was issued, which amended the previous notification to include block-list items in the PSI exemptions.

qa_pairs.question: What significant revisions to PSI fee structures and importer responsibilities were introduced one year after the 2012-06-27 amendment?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2013-06-06, SRO 151/2013 was issued, revising the PSI fee structures based on CIF value and updating the responsibilities of importers, including the requirement to specify an inspection agency when opening a Letter of Credit.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the Advance Ruling System, what procedural detail was added three days later to the initial establishment of the Advance Ruling Unit?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2016-06-05, the Advance Ruling Rules were updated to include specific procedural details, such as the requirement to submit applications directly, by post, courier, email, or fax, and the mandate that the Advance Ruling Unit must finalize applications within 45 working days.

qa_pairs.question: On June 10, 2010, the government issued several customs notifications. Four years later, on June 5, 2014, S.R.O. 128-AIN/2014/2492/Customs was issued. Under which section of the Customs Act 1969 was this 2014 S.R.O. issued, which previous notification did it amend, and what specific H.S. Code substitution was made?
qa_pairs.answer: S.R.O. 128-AIN/2014/2492/Customs was issued under Section 20 of the Customs Act 1969. It amended the notification S.R.O. 74-AIN/2005/2067/Customs (originally dated March 28, 2005). The amendment substituted the H.S. Code '7307.99.00' with '7307.99.90' in column (2) of the TABLE in part 'Ka' ('ক') of the notification.

qa_pairs.question: On June 9, 2011, S.R.O. 158-AIN/2011/2344/Customs was issued regarding exemptions from mandatory pre-shipment inspections. One year later, on June 7, 2012, a new S.R.O. was issued that repealed this 2011 notification. What is the number of this 2012 S.R.O., and under what specific legal provision of the Customs Act 1969 was it issued?
qa_pairs.answer: The 2012 notification is S.R.O. 178-AIN/2012/2406/Customs. It was issued under the authority of the proviso to Section 25B of the Customs Act 1969.

qa_pairs.question: On June 10, 2010, S.R.O. 190-AIN/2010/2308/Customs was issued regarding valuation conditions. Three years later, on June 6, 2013, S.R.O. 158-AIN/2013/2445/Customs was issued. What previous S.R.O. did this 2013 notification amend, and what specific date substitution did it make in condition (b)?
qa_pairs.answer: S.R.O. 158-AIN/2013/2445/Customs amended S.R.O. 325-AIN/2000/1872/Customs (dated October 26, 2000). In condition (b), it substituted '30 June, 2013' with '30 June, 2014'.

qa_pairs.question: On June 9, 2011, S.R.O. 157-AIN/2011/2343/Customs was issued. Three years later, on June 5, 2014, S.R.O. 134-AIN/2014/2498/Customs was issued to amend it. What specific substitution was made under Heading 85.28 of the TABLE in S.R.O. 157-AIN/2011/2343/Customs by this 2014 amendment?
qa_pairs.answer: Under Heading 85.28 of the TABLE, for the H.S. Code '8528.51.10' in column (2), the number '22' in column (3) was substituted with the number '19'.

qa_pairs.question: Six years after the issuance of SRO 185-AIN/2010/2303/Customs on June 10, 2010, the government issued SRO 169-AIN/2016/31/Customs to further amend SRO 11-AIN/2005/2063/Customs. Under clause (ক) of this later 2016 SRO, what specific H.S. Code substitution was made in the Table of 'Part A'?
qa_pairs.answer: Under SRO 169-AIN/2016/31/Customs, the H.S. Code "7307.99.00" (which was mentioned twice in column 2 against Sl. No. 14 and 15 of the Table in 'Part A') was replaced in both places with H.S. Code "7307.99.90".

qa_pairs.question: Three years after SRO 171-AIN/2011/2358/Customs was issued on June 9, 2011, the government issued SRO 134-AIN/2014/2498/Customs. What specific numerical replacement did this 2014 SRO make in the Table under Heading 85.28 against H.S. Code "8528.51.10"?
qa_pairs.answer: In SRO 134-AIN/2014/2498/Customs, the number "22" in column (3) against H.S. Code "8528.51.10" was replaced with the number "19".

qa_pairs.question: Three years after SRO 166-AIN/2012/2394/Customs was issued on June 7, 2012, the government issued SRO 156-AIN/2015/36/Customs to amend SRO 169-AIN/2005/2078/Customs. What specific H.S. Code substitutions were made in the Table of the 2005 notification by this 2015 SRO?
qa_pairs.answer:
SRO 156-AIN/2015/36/Customs substituted the following H.S. Codes in the Table:
(ক) "3204.13.00" was replaced with "3204.13.90"
(খ) "3206.19.00" was replaced with "3206.19.90"

qa_pairs.question: One year before the updates in SRO 135-AIN/2017 (issued on June 1, 2017) which inserted H.S. Codes like "1901.90.20", the government issued SRO 173-AIN/2016/35/Customs. What specific H.S. Code substitution did this 2016 SRO make against Heading 29.33 in the Table of SRO 203-AIN/2015/40/Customs?
qa_pairs.answer: SRO 173-AIN/2016/35/Customs substituted H.S. Code "2933.39.90" with H.S. Code "2933.39.00" against Heading 29.33 in the Table of SRO 203-AIN/2015/40/Customs.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial imposition of 10% Regulatory Duty on rice in May 2015, what regulatory change regarding Regulatory Duty occurred about three months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2015-08-26, via SRO 276/2015, the government imposed a 20% Regulatory Duty on sugar.

qa_pairs.question: Following the imposition of RD on sugar in August 2015, what action was taken regarding specific industrial inputs roughly three months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2015-11-29, via SRO 353/2015, the government imposed a Regulatory Duty on copper-based products, including bars, plates, and tubes.

qa_pairs.question: After the refinement of RD on rice varieties in December 2015, what major regulatory shift occurred the following year?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2016-07-01, via SRO 223/2016, the government implemented a general adjustment of Regulatory Duty rates for various commodities.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the Government relied on Section 19(1) of the Customs Act 1969 to issue notifications; five years later, what legal framework was additionally cited in conjunction with the Customs Act 1969 for issuing customs notifications?
qa_pairs.answer: By 2015-06-04 (SRO 140-Ain/2015), the Government began reading Section 19(1) of the Customs Act 1969 in conjunction with Section 14(1) of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 to issue or amend customs notifications.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the legal basis for issuing customs notifications, how did the regulatory authority change four years after the issuance of SRO 127-Ain/2020?
qa_pairs.answer: Four years later, in 2024 (as evidenced by SRO 230-Ain/2024), the Government transitioned from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023 as the primary legal basis (specifically Section 25(1)) for issuing notifications and amendments, while continuing to utilize Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.

qa_pairs.relative_offset: a little over one year later
qa_pairs.question: Following the Customs Policy Directive introduced on 2024-03-31, what regulatory development occurred a little over one year later regarding the government's power to amend existing rules for export-oriented industries?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-06-02, the government issued SRO No. 235-Ain/2025/57/Customs, which serves as the enabling legislation under the Customs Act 2023 for the National Board of Revenue to formally set rules regarding annual import entitlements for direct and deemed export-oriented industries (excluding the apparel sector).

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the Commissioner was designated as the authority for receiving usage certificates; what change in the Commissioner's authority occurred six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-06-02 (SRO 157-AIN/2016), the Commissioner's authority was expanded to include licensing and the responsibility for annual input requirement verification for manufacturers.

qa_pairs.question: Following the formal definition of the Commissioner role in 2019-01-21, what significant operational authority was granted to the Commissioner three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2022-06-09 (SRO 2022), the Commissioner was granted discretionary power to allow for manual customs clearance in the event of electronic system failures.

qa_pairs.question: Seven years after the issuance of SRO 146/2013, what significant regulatory change was introduced regarding how repealed minimum values are treated in customs valuation?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2020-06-11 (SRO 132/2020), the government formalized the rule that repealed minimum values must be considered in current valuations, and introduced the provision allowing authorities to set a higher assessable value based on factors like brand, model, and country of origin.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the 2020 formalization of valuation rules, what specific instruction was provided in 2021-06-03 regarding the application of the Customs Valuation Rules 2000 in relation to previous minimum price references?
qa_pairs.answer: SRO 133/2021 clarified that the Customs Valuation Rules 2000 serve as the primary mechanism for goods without a fixed minimum price, and mandated that these rules must be applied in conjunction with historical minimum price references from repealed notifications.

qa_pairs.question: Three years after the initial duty concessions were introduced in 2010, what specific expert verification requirement was mandated for ship and dredger construction materials?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2013, under SRO 147/2013, the government introduced a requirement for mandatory expert opinion from the Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Department of BUET to verify the quantity of materials used in ship or dredger construction.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the introduction of strict industrial usage verification and scrap disposal rules in 2016, how did the monitoring framework expand regarding specific industrial sectors?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2017, under SRO 134/2017, the scope of monitoring was expanded to include specific sectors such as animal feed, computers, and mobile phones, with strict prohibitions on transferring or selling imported components for unauthorized purposes.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the 2021 refinement of the committee-based verification process, what new requirement was introduced in 2022 regarding the monitoring of appliance manufacturing like refrigerators and ACs?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2022, under SRO 122/2022, the government introduced the standardization of Input-Output Coefficient (IOCO) submissions and mandated committee-based monitoring to ensure compliance for the production of appliances like refrigerators and air conditioners.

qa_pairs.question: In 2016-06-02, SRO 160/2016 formalized VAT-7 form submissions. What major change regarding VAT registration and electronic verification was mandated six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, on 2022-06-09, SRO 118/2022 mandated that entities must hold a 13-digit BIN and undergo electronic verification of monthly VAT returns via online systems as a prerequisite for customs clearance.

qa_pairs.question: SRO 169-199/2024 (issued 2024-06-06) required 13-digit VAT registration for duty-free imports. What new enforcement role for VAT commissioners was introduced one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2025-06-02, SRO 193-201/2025 introduced mandatory audit and verification roles for VAT commissioners to specifically monitor entities receiving fiscal benefits and enforce penalties.

qa_pairs.question: Five years after the initial exemption framework of 2010 was established, what significant expansion of the VAT exemption scope was introduced in the 2015 regulatory order?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2015 (SRO 208/2015), the exemption scope was expanded to include industrial factories located in Economic Zones and High-Tech Parks, allowing them to import raw materials or manufacturing inputs under a bonded warehouse system.

qa_pairs.question: Four years after the 2015 extension of exemptions to high-tech parks, what major shift occurred regarding the legal basis for VAT exemptions?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2019 (SRO 256/2019), the legal basis for VAT exemptions shifted from the VAT Act 1991 to the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after the transition to the 2012 Act legal basis in 2019, what action was taken regarding the consolidation of exemption clauses?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2021 (SRO 113/2021), the government formally consolidated exemption clauses under the authority of the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

qa_pairs.question: Five years later, what standardization measure was introduced regarding duty exemptions for industrial inputs?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2015-06-04, SRO 145/2015 was issued, which established the standardization of a 5% excess duty exemption for industrial inputs.

qa_pairs.question: One month later, what significant change was made to the percentage-based partial exemptions established under the new Customs Act 2023 framework?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-07-08, SRO 249/2024 was issued, which amended previous SROs to replace percentage-based partial exemptions with full duty exemptions.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial establishment of minimum value for motor vehicles in 2010, what significant change occurred one year later regarding the scope of tariff values?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2011, specifically on June 9, 2011, SRO 159/2011 expanded the application of tariff values to include a wider range of goods, and SRO 167-Law/2011 introduced specific minimum value thresholds for used and reconditioned motor vehicles.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2013 update to minimum value determinations for new motor vehicles, what major shift in enforcement occurred seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven years later, on June 11, 2020, SRO 135/2020 was issued, which formalized the minimum value as the mandatory dutiable value for customs assessment purposes.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2010 introduction of Green/Red channel baggage rules, what significant regulatory change regarding customs agents occurred six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-06-02, the Customs Agent Rules were introduced, which established specific penalties for duty evasion committed by customs agents.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the implementation of detailed schedules for baggage duty in 2022, what major procedural shift was introduced regarding customs audit operations?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2023-09-27, the Audit Manual was introduced, shifting the focus toward risk-based audits and formalizing recovery procedures for customs compliance.

qa_pairs.question: Ten years after the 2010 issuance of SRO 169-192/2010, what major regulatory action was taken regarding legacy notifications?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2020, specifically under SRO 120-163/2020, a mass revocation of legacy notifications spanning from 1995 to 2019 was executed to streamline the regulatory framework.

qa_pairs.question: Three years after the implementation of SRO 116-137/2022, what significant legal transition occurred regarding the issuance and repeal of customs notifications?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025, with the issuance of SRO 236-247/2025, the legal basis for notification issuance and repeal transitioned from the Customs Act, 1969 to the Customs Act, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the framework established on 2024-06-06, what major regulatory development occurred about three months later concerning the import of raw materials for ship and dredger building?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-09-12, the NBR issued Order 60/2024, which introduced specific procedures for importing raw materials under international tenders specifically for ship and dredger building.

qa_pairs.question: Following the NBR Directive on 2024-09-24, what significant change in compliance documentation was implemented four months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the Audit Rules were introduced, which integrated system-based audit reporting for bonded entities, marking a shift toward automated, system-based compliance.

qa_pairs.question: What expansion of import facilities for non-licensed entities was introduced nearly four months after the sector-specific duty exemptions of 2025-06-02?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-09-29, SRO 384/2025 was issued, which introduced bank guarantee-based import facilities for non-licensed warehouse entities and established strict export timelines.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010, the duty-free baggage allowance for land passengers was set at $300 USD. How did this specific allowance value change six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, on 2016-04-08, the baggage rules were updated to increase the duty-free allowance for land passengers from $300 USD to $400 USD.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the land passenger baggage allowance established in 2016, what regulatory constraint was introduced seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven years later, on 2023-06-01, the baggage rules were amended to introduce a frequency limit, restricting passengers to availing the duty-free allowance no more than 3 times per calendar year.

qa_pairs.question: Seven years later, how did the framework for post-clearance audits change regarding the selection of auditees and the recovery of underpaid taxes?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023-09-27, the Customs Audit Manual was formalized, shifting the process to a risk-based selection system using automated software and intelligence, and establishing Section 83A of the Customs Act as the legal framework for issuing standardized demand notices for the recovery of short-paid duties and taxes.

qa_pairs.question: What procedural update occurred the following year regarding the reassessment of goods and the recovery of duties?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-06, the Customs Rules were updated to formalize reassessment procedures, requiring officials to document the grounds for reassessment when recovering additional duties, taxes, or fees, or when refunds were granted in error.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the mandate for digital registration on February 17, 2025, what requirement was introduced three months later regarding transit and transshipment shipments?
qa_pairs.answer: On May 18, 2025, the Customs Rules 2025 established that each transit or transshipment shipment requires an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee from a scheduled bank in Bangladesh to mitigate revenue risks.

qa_pairs.question: Following the transit guarantee requirements established on May 18, 2025, what specific regulatory changes were introduced approximately two weeks later regarding duty exemptions and cargo declarations?
qa_pairs.answer: On June 2, 2025, SRO 200-Law/2025 was issued, which implemented specific duty exemptions for industrial molds and medical equipment and formalized digital cargo declaration procedures.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the baseline established on June 6, 2024, regarding electronic payment mandates, what significant development occurred about seven months later concerning the formalization of payment facilities for AEO-certified entities?
qa_pairs.answer: On January 21, 2025, the Customs Automation Directive was issued, which formalized deferred payment facilities specifically for AEO-certified entities linked to automated systems.

qa_pairs.question: Building upon the procedural mandates introduced on June 6, 2024, what major update regarding duty rates and risk-based physical examination protocols was implemented exactly one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: On June 2, 2025, SRO 192-209/2025 was issued, which refined duty rates for industrial raw material imports and established specific conditions for risk-based physical examination protocols.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010, the SRO implementation framework was established; what significant shift in the 'effective date' mechanism occurred three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, in 2013, SRO 159-Law/2013 introduced the mechanism of retrospective effective dates for statutory regulatory orders.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2013 introduction of retrospective effective dates, what change regarding the implementation of regulatory orders was introduced six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years after 2013, on January 21, 2019, an Order was issued that introduced the concept of 'immediate effect' for SROs upon their issuance.

qa_pairs.question: After the standardization of sunset clauses in 2020, what development in the application of these clauses occurred four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Four years later, on June 6, 2024, SRO 227-Law/2024 was issued, marking a shift toward the systematic use of multi-year sunset clauses.

qa_pairs.question: In the year following the initial 2010 batch of exemptions, what specific regulatory action was taken under Section 19(1) regarding industrial inputs?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2011-06-09, via SRO 151-172/2011, the government broadened exemptions and updated HS codes specifically for industrial inputs.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the 2015 consolidation of exemptions, what major structural shift occurred in the duty exemption regime for local manufacturing?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2016-06-02, via SRO 145-173/2016, the government implemented a major restructuring of duty exemptions specifically targeting local manufacturing sectors such as motorcycles and electronics.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the 2017 refinement of HS codes, what action was taken by the government regarding the notification issued on 21 June 2017?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2018-06-07, via SRO 143-2018, the government exercised its authority under Section 19(1) to formally repeal the notification that had been issued on 21 June 2017.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of the Customs Act 1969, how did the operational requirements for the Appropriate Officer of Customs evolve 55 years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-06-03, the NBR introduced specific operational forms and certification procedures, shifting the Appropriate Officer's role from general statutory authority to a system defined by digitized operational workflows, such as mandatory container management and passenger baggage declarations.

qa_pairs.question: In 2018-06-28, the AEO program operated under a committee-led model. What major structural change to the governance framework occurred six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the AEO Rules 2024 were issued, which formally created the AEO Center and expanded the committee's governance scope, marking a shift from a committee-led model to a centralized AEO Center model.

qa_pairs.question: Following the establishment of the AEO Center in 2024-06-13, what specific operational and administrative developments were introduced the following year?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, a Standing Order was issued that operationalized the Center's staffing, secretarial support, and established formal operational templates, reporting protocols, and procedures for processing AEO applications and dispute resolution.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the baseline AEO Rules 2018, what significant structural change to the AEO system was introduced six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In June 2024, the AEO Rules 2024 were introduced, which transitioned the system from a single-tier status to a multi-tiered framework consisting of Tier 1-3 and Logistics Operator categories, along with formal application and renewal protocols.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024 AEO Rules implemented in mid-2024, what specific operational details were further formalized eight months later?
qa_pairs.answer: By February 2025 (specifically February 17, 2025), the AEO (Recognition and Operation) Rules 2024 were operationalized to include standardized forms for all lifecycle stages, specific audit requirements, and a defined classification structure for promotion to Tier-3 status.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of System Based Audit guidelines in September 2023, what new operational requirements were introduced for AEOs less than nine months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the AEO Rules 2024 were issued, which mandated the use of electronic seals and locks on containers or vehicles and introduced annual onsite performance evaluations.

qa_pairs.question: What significant changes regarding the audit and enforcement powers of customs authorities were introduced about seven months after the AEO Rules 2024 were established?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, a Standing Order was issued that strengthened audit enforcement by authorizing intelligence-led inspections, mandatory cross-departmental reporting of irregularities, and random risk-based audits to ensure compliance.

qa_pairs.question: Exactly one week after the introduction of comprehensive guarantees for AEOs, what new legal foundation was formalized regarding international cooperation?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the AEO Rules 2024 were issued, providing the formal legal basis for the National Board of Revenue to enter into Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) with other countries.

qa_pairs.question: Seven months after the formalization of Mutual Recognition Agreements in the AEO Rules 2024, what specific action did the Board take to operationalize these agreements?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, a Standing Order was issued authorizing the Board to sign MRAs with foreign customs administrations and issue directives to implement such agreements under the AEO programme.

qa_pairs.question: Bangladesh ratified the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement in 2016; what happened one year later regarding this agreement?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2017, following approval by two-thirds of the member states, the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement officially came into effect.

qa_pairs.question: In 2023-05-21, amendments were issued under the Customs Act, 1969. What significant change regarding the legal basis for issuing regulatory notifications occurred one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2024-06-26, the legal basis for issuing regulatory notifications transitioned from the Customs Act, 1969 to the Customs Act, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Following the issuance of SROs 231, 235, and 208 in 2024-06-26, what was the status of the regulatory framework one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2025-05-29, the government continued to utilize the Customs Act, 2023 as the legal authority for issuing ongoing regulatory adjustments and notifications.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial establishment of exemptions under the Customs Act 2023 framework on June 6, 2024, what major expansion occurred one year later regarding the scope of these exemptions?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on June 2, 2025 (SRO 190-218/2025), the government broadly expanded exemptions to include new sectors such as E-bikes and Lithium batteries, while simultaneously rescinding older, redundant notifications.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of the Customs Rules 2025 on February 17, 2025, what major regulatory framework was established three months later concerning transit and transshipment operations?
qa_pairs.answer: On May 18, 2025, the Transit/Transshipment Rules 2025 were introduced, formalizing inter-agency coordination, implementing electronic sealing, and establishing risk-based physical examination protocols for transit goods.

qa_pairs.question: In 2022, electronic verification of BINs was introduced; what enforcement change occurred two years later regarding BIN status and bonded warehouse operations?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024, the Bonded Warehouse Rules were updated to link BIN status directly to legal enforcement, allowing authorities to suspend a licensee's BIN and operational licenses if they fail to submit required documents or comply with audits.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024 linkage of BIN status to license suspension, what procedural shift regarding BIN errors in cargo declarations was introduced one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025, the Cargo Declaration Rules classified BIN errors in cargo declarations as serious procedural violations, requiring formal approval from a senior official for any related amendments.

qa_pairs.question: In 2017, the BIN was standardized for factory inspection reports; seven years later, how was the BIN integrated into the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) framework?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, with the AEO Rules 2024, the BIN was integrated into the AEO lifecycle, requiring applicants to provide an updated BIN and branch-specific registration details for centralized entities as part of the formal application and affidavit process.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024 AEO Rules, what administrative expansion regarding BIN usage and AEO registry management occurred a few months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the AEO Operational Guidelines were introduced, which expanded the usage of the BIN into intelligence reporting and formal AEO registry management.

qa_pairs.question: In the Baggage Rules 2010, the definition of baggage was limited to reasonable quantities of personal effects. How did the definition change six years later in the subsequent rules?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2016 (June 2, 2016), the definition was updated to include a quantitative constraint: no individual item of baggage could exceed a weight limit of 15kg.

qa_pairs.question: The Baggage Rules 2016 introduced a 15kg weight limit per individual item. What was the status of this threshold seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2023 (June 1, 2023), the 15kg per item weight threshold was reaffirmed and maintained as part of the baggage definition.

qa_pairs.question: In the Baggage Rules 2010, the duty-free allowance for land route passengers was set at 300 USD; how did this limit change six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2016 (April 8, 2016), the duty-free allowance for land route passengers was increased from 300 USD to 400 USD.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 update which set the land route duty-free baggage allowance to 400 USD, what new restriction was introduced seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2023 (June 1, 2023), while the monetary limit was maintained at 400 USD, a frequency restriction was introduced, limiting passengers to using the duty-free allowance a maximum of 3 times per calendar year.

qa_pairs.question: In the Baggage Rules 2010, the crew baggage allowance was set at 100 USD. How did this allowance change six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2016 (dated 2016-04-08), the crew allowance was increased to 300 USD.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 increase of the crew baggage allowance to 300 USD, what adjustment was made to this allowance nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2025 (dated 2025-06-03), the crew baggage allowance was adjusted downward to 150 USD.

qa_pairs.question: In the Baggage Rules 2010, the declaration window for unaccompanied baggage was 21 days; how did this requirement change two years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2012, enacted on 2012-06-07, the declaration window was reduced from 21 days to 3 days.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 3-day declaration window established in 2012, what adjustment was made to the baggage declaration timeframe four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the Baggage Rules 2016, enacted on 2016-06-02, the declaration window was increased from 3 days to 7 days.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2010 establishment of the 1% excess threshold for industrial machinery, what change occurred one year later regarding machinery and component duty thresholds?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2011-06-09, SRO 156/2011 was issued, which introduced a 3% excess threshold for industrial machinery and components.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the standardization of the 1% excess threshold in 2016, what specific sector-based duty adjustment was introduced five years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2021-06-03, SRO 125/2021 was issued, which applied a 5% threshold specifically for local washing machine production.

qa_pairs.question: After the 2021 introduction of the 5% threshold for washing machines, what policy change regarding industrial production was implemented four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-02, SRO 200/2025 was issued, which applied a 1% threshold for local industrial mould and die production.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the formalization of duty-free status in 2015, what significant change occurred nearly nine years later regarding the legal framework governing duty and tax exemptions for industrial units in economic zones?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-06, via SRO 184/2024, the legal basis for granting duty and tax exemptions to industrial units in economic zones was updated from the Customs Act, 1969 to the Customs Act, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of duty drawback procedures in 2021, what procedural change regarding cargo declaration and duty payment was introduced nearly four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-02, under SRO 2025, specific provisions were introduced to facilitate cargo declaration and duty payment within the digital system, including allowances for declarations based on transport documents when single-entry electronic filing is not possible.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the government established a broad exemption for machinery and parts. What significant change occurred five years later regarding the duty threshold and conditions for these parts?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, in 2015-06-04 (SRO 145-AIN/2015), the framework introduced specific conditions for imports and established a 5% duty threshold for parts.

qa_pairs.question: Following the formalization of Input-Output Coefficient (IOC) requirements in 2017-06-01, what major structural change to manufacturer classification for specific industries was introduced five years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, in 2022-06-09 (SRO 120/139/143-AIN/2022), the regulatory framework introduced 'Category-1' and 'Category-2' manufacturer classifications for specific industries.

qa_pairs.question: In 2022-06-09, the Customs Act 1969 served as the primary legal basis for industrial import concessions. What shift in the legal framework occurred two years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Two years later, in 2024-06-06 (SRO 194-AIN/2024), the regulatory framework transitioned from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the codification of temporary import procedures in 2022, what major regulatory change occurred three years later regarding the framework for the temporary importation of goods, machinery, and parts?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, on June 2, 2025, the Temporary Import Rules 2025 were introduced, which officially repealed the 2022 rules while maintaining the regulatory framework for returnable imports.

qa_pairs.question: Three years after the initial duty exemption framework of 2010 was established, what new requirement was introduced for the verification of specific industrial materials?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2013, with the issuance of SRO 153-AIN/2013, a mandatory expert team (BUET) verification was introduced for the verification of specific industrial materials.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after the standardization of input-output coefficient declarations in 2017, how did the approval process for these coefficients evolve under the 2019 SRO?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2019, SRO 2019 refined the approval process for input-output coefficients, specifically requiring the VAT Commissioner to form a committee led by an official not below the rank of Joint Commissioner to conduct mandatory field inspections.

qa_pairs.question: Three years after the 2021 expansion of committee-based oversight to digital products, what major regulatory integration occurred regarding audit reporting for material usage?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024, SRO 2024 integrated the Customs Act 2023 and introduced standardized audit reporting, known as System Based Audit, for the verification of material usage.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of the initial AEO framework in 2018-06-28, what major structural change to the application and recognition system was introduced six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, the AEO Rules 2024 (issued on 2024-06-13) introduced a multi-tiered (Tier-1, Tier-2, and Tier-3) system for AEO status and established formal documentation for application rejection and acceptance.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of the 2024 AEO Rules on 2024-06-13, what specific procedural refinements regarding audit teams and rejection criteria were implemented seven months later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven months later, on 2025-01-21, the AEO Operational Directives were issued, which refined audit procedures by mandating Assessment Teams to review applications and Self-Assessment Questionnaires, while also establishing formal notification requirements for application cancellations.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial establishment of the Advance Ruling Rules on 2016-06-02, what significant procedural addition was introduced three days later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2016-06-05, the Advance Ruling Rules 2016 (Amendment) was introduced, which established review mechanisms for aggrieved applicants and defined detailed processing timelines for the Advance Ruling Unit.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016-06-05 amendment, what major digital and submission updates were implemented nearly nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-06-02, the Advance Ruling Rules Amendment was enacted, which mandated the use of e-Challan for fee payments and expanded the submission channels to include email, fax, and courier services.

qa_pairs.question: In 2016-06-02, the Customs Agent Licensing Rules introduced electronic or manual submission methods. How did the legal framework for electronic document submission change eight years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-06-06, the Customs (Electronic Submission) Rules were introduced, providing a formal definition of electronic records, signatures, and electronic payment systems for document submission.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024-06-06 Customs (Electronic Submission) Rules, what major mandate regarding electronic document submission was introduced the following year?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the AEO Rules were issued, mandating electronic submission for Green Lane clearance.

qa_pairs.question: A few months after the 2025-01-21 AEO Rules mandated electronic submissions for Green Lane, how did the Customs Rules further evolve the definition of documents?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-03-10, the Customs Rules expanded the definition of documents to include any information stored in physical, electronic, or other media.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the Post Clearance Audit Guidelines established in 2023-09-27, what significant expansion in audit authority occurred six months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-03-31, the Customs Rules were updated to empower the National Board of Revenue to establish committees and engage professional auditors or firms to monitor and audit the documents and operations of service providers.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 rules that formalized the Licensing Authority and NBR approval, what change was introduced eight years later regarding the jurisdictional scope of a customs license?
qa_pairs.answer: In the 2024-06-06 Customs Agent Licensing Rules, it was clarified that licenses are strictly tied to the jurisdiction of the specific Customs House or station, and this scope must be explicitly stated on the license.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016-06-02 directive that established the requirement for annual production plans, what major shift in the audit structure occurred seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023-09-27, the Audit Policy introduced a formal system-based and transaction-based audit structure, tasking Customs Houses with conducting transaction-based post-clearance audits.

qa_pairs.question: Following the Perishable Goods Management Rules established on 2021-08-29, what significant regulatory change regarding the handling of high-value items like gold and liquor occurred nearly four months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2021-12-20, the Disposal Order was issued, which standardized the handling of high-value items (such as gold and liquor) and established professional panels for valuation, requiring these items to be transferred to the Bangladesh Bank.

qa_pairs.question: In 2016-06-02, customs verification relied on basic electronic communication like phone, fax, or email. What significant change to the documentation and payment process occurred eight years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Eight years later, in 2024-06-06, SRO 191-Law/2024 mandated the electronic submission of all declarations and the use of electronic payment systems for all customs duties, taxes, and associated fees.

qa_pairs.question: Following the mandate for electronic submission and payment in 2024-06-06, what formalization regarding audit-related communication occurred seven months later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven months later, on 2025-01-21, the Audit Manual formalized the use of written communication or email for audit teams to request additional information or documentation from an auditee's focal point officer.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the 2023-09-27 PCA Manual, what procedural change regarding AEO documentation deficiencies was introduced less than a year later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the AEO Center Directive was issued, which standardized formal templates for notifying applicants of deficiencies in their provided documentation or information.

qa_pairs.question: Following the AEO Center Directive of 2024-06-13, what major expansion to the AEO documentation and status requirements occurred eight months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-02-16, the AEO Guidelines were introduced, which established the application process for Tier-3 status and mandated detailed documentation for IT outsourcing.

qa_pairs.relative_offset: one year and four months later
qa_pairs.question: Following the 2023-09-27 PCA Manual, how did the documentation process evolve one year and four months later regarding the timelines for document requests and evaluation procedures?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the PCA Manual Update introduced refinements to document request timelines and audit evaluation procedures, including specific provisions for Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) status applications and consequences for failing to submit requested documentation within prescribed timeframes.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the 2017-06-01 SRO which established the Commissioner as the primary authority for input-output coefficient approvals, how did the inspection procedure change two years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the 2019-05-30 SRO, the inspection process evolved from direct Commissioner oversight to a formal committee-led structure, where physical inspections were conducted by a committee led by an official no lower than a Joint Commissioner.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2021-06-03 SRO that expanded committee-based inspection models to new industries, what new reporting requirement was introduced one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the 2022-06-09 SRO, the system introduced annual estimation requirements and mandated the use of standardized reporting formats, specifically replacing the existing documentation with a new Appendix-3 (পরিশিষ্ট-৩) for audit compliance.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after the 2022-06-09 SRO introduced standardized reporting formats like Appendix-3, how did the compliance and estimation process evolve?
qa_pairs.answer: In the 2024-06-06 SRO, the process was refined to require manufacturers to estimate annual input quantities based on the previous year's production and capacity, submitting these calculations to the Commissioner by January each year.

qa_pairs.question: In 2018-06-28, the AEO program was overseen by a committee chaired by the Commissioner. Six years later, what major structural change occurred regarding the governance of the AEO program?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the AEO Center was created, shifting governance from the initial committee to a centralized center and mandating the nomination of a Commissioner-rank officer as Director General.

qa_pairs.question: Following the creation of the AEO Center in 2024-06-13, what significant integration occurred nine months later concerning the Commissioner's role in risk management?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-03-10, the Commissioner was integrated into the newly formed central Integrated Risk Management Committee (IRMC) to fulfill the objectives of the Customs Risk Management Rules 2025.

qa_pairs.question: In 2012, SRO 175-AIN/2012 established a mechanism for amending SROs; what procedural change was introduced exactly one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, in 2013, SRO 143-AIN/2013 formalized the procedure for the outright cancellation or repeal of previous regulatory notifications.

qa_pairs.question: SRO 151-AIN/2019 focused on refining the amendment process through H.S. Code entries; what significant shift in the legal basis for repealing legacy notifications occurred six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, in 2025, SRO 242-AIN/2025 was issued, which adopted the Customs Act, 2023 as the primary legal basis for repealing legacy notifications dating back to 2008.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the formalization of automated decisions in the Customs Rules 2024, what major integration regarding AEO status and payment facilities occurred seven months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the AEO Operational Guidelines were introduced, integrating AEO status management, deferred payment schemes (7 or 14 days), and automated risk management lanes.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of AEO Operational Guidelines in early 2025, what specific provision regarding cargo declaration procedures was introduced four months later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-06-02, the Customs Rules 2025 were issued, which standardized cargo declaration segments and introduced specific provisions for submitting declarations based on transport documents when single electronic entry is not possible.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of the committee-based application procedure in 2018, how did the AEO application process change six years later regarding institutional oversight and transparency?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024 (specifically June 13, 2024, under AEO Rules 2024), the process shifted from a general committee to a specialized AEO Center with structured evaluation teams and introduced formal notification forms for deficiencies and rejections.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of the AEO Center in 2024, what major operational advancements were implemented the following year regarding application processing and tier-upgrades?
qa_pairs.answer: In early 2025 (January and February), the system was further operationalized through detailed checklists for tier-upgrades, the integration of electronic systems for drawback processing, and the standardization of specific application forms for receipt, rejection, and tier-upgrades.

qa_pairs.question: In 2016-06-02, the Advance Ruling Rules were established; how did the processing of these applications change nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-02, the rules were updated to explicitly standardize the processing timeline to 45 working days and emphasize electronic communication methods for the disposal of applications.

qa_pairs.question: Eight years after the 2015 Customs Rules explicitly defined 'person' to include companies and partnerships, how did the scope of this term change in the 2023 Customs Audit Directive?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023, the Customs Audit Directive expanded the scope of 'person' to include specific business roles such as Authorized Economic Operators (AEOs), custodians, and declarants for the purpose of audit accountability.

qa_pairs.question: In the following year, how did the 2024 Baggage Rules further refine the application of the term 'person' or related entities within the customs framework?
qa_pairs.answer: The 2024 Baggage Rules introduced specific exclusions for 'privileged persons' and 'tourists' regarding the applicability of the baggage framework.

qa_pairs.question: In 2012, the SRO structure was limited to a standard effective date declaration. How did the regulatory instrument issued four years later evolve regarding its effective date application?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016, the SRO evolved to introduce a retrospective effective date, allowing the instrument to be deemed effective from a past date rather than just a standard forward-looking date.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 introduction of retrospective application clauses, what significant change was introduced in the SRO issued eight years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024, the regulatory framework introduced explicit validity periods or expiry dates alongside the effective dates, marking a shift toward temporary measures with defined lifespans.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2013-06-06 amendment that established a 10-day window for amending certificates, how did the procedural timeframe for filing administrative review applications change nearly 12 years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-02, under the Customs Ruling (Advance) Rules, 2025, the timeframe for filing and disposing of administrative review applications was established as 60 days.

qa_pairs.question: Given the importer responsibilities defined on June 6, 2013, what regulatory change occurred less than one month later regarding PSI agency interactions?
qa_pairs.answer: On July 1, 2013, through SRO 219-2013, the government introduced a tiered fee structure for importers to pay PSI agencies based on CIF value, amending the existing pre-shipment inspection rules.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of the tiered PSI fee structure in 2013, what significant policy shift occurred over ten years later regarding customs compliance?
qa_pairs.answer: On September 27, 2023, the NBR issued a directive shifting the customs focus from pre-shipment inspection to post-clearance audit (PCA) and risk-based selection criteria for importers.

qa_pairs.relative_offset: about one and a half years later
qa_pairs.question: After the 2023 directive on post-clearance audits, what advancement in customs risk management occurred about one and a half years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On March 10, 2025, the Customs Rules formalized an automated selectivity framework, classifying consignments into Red, Yellow, Blue, and Green lanes to manage risks based on pre-defined indicators.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the initial concessional duty framework was established. Six years later, what major changes were introduced regarding the requirements for manufacturer-importers?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-06-02 (SRO 2016), the framework introduced strict registration, mandatory progress reporting, and increased monitoring requirements for manufacturer-importers.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the monitoring of importers, what new certification mandate was introduced eight years after the 2016-06-02 regulatory update?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-06-06 (SRO 2024), the framework mandated that importers obtain certification from both local VAT offices and the banks that issued their L/Cs to qualify for duty concessions.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the 2024-06-06 mandate for VAT and bank certification, what new enforcement measure was added to the concessional duty framework?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-02 (SRO 2025), the framework was strengthened by allowing authorities to suspend duty concessions if there is evidence of misuse by the importer.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of the Advance Ruling Rules on 2016-06-02, what change occurred three days later regarding the usage of these rulings by other importers?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2016-06-05, the Advance Ruling Rules were updated to allow other importers to use existing rulings as a reference for the customs assessment of identical goods.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016-06-05 expansion of the reference-based ruling system, what occurred nearly nine years later regarding the eligibility and compliance framework for advance rulings?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-06-02, the Advance Ruling Rules were updated to reaffirm the mandatory compliance requirements for ruling holders and customs stations, and to explicitly re-state the eligibility criteria for importers and exporters to apply for advance rulings.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of formal rejection procedures for AEO applications on February 16, 2025, what regulatory development occurred one day later regarding the status of AEO participants?
qa_pairs.answer: On February 17, 2025, the AEO Rules 2024 established formal certification protocols (Recognition Certificate) and procedures for granting time extensions to AEOs to fulfill their recognition conditions.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the refinement of tariff value lists in June 2022, what specific update occurred one month later regarding raw sugar?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2022-07-17, SRO 203/2022 was issued, which provided updated tariff values specifically for raw sugar.

qa_pairs.question: Following the consolidation of minimum value lists under the new Customs Act 2023 in June 2024, what major change took place one month later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-07-08, SRO 230/2024 was issued, which comprehensively replaced TABLE-2 with updated minimum values for food and industrial goods.

qa_pairs.question: In the context of industrial raw material concessions, what specific compliance protocols were introduced for pesticide and electric motor manufacturers three years after the introduction of annual production planning requirements in 2022?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, in 2025 (SRO 192/2025), the government introduced strict certification and compliance protocols, requiring manufacturers to be VAT-compliant and hold a valid Industrial Consumer Import Registration Certificate (IRC) issued by the Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after the 2022 refinement of H.S. Codes for electronics and ceramics (SRO 201/2022), what major legislative change occurred regarding the authority for granting customs duty concessions?
qa_pairs.answer: Two years later, in 2024 (SRO 164/2024), the regulatory framework was updated to align with the newly enacted Customs Act 2023, which replaced the previous legal foundations and established new duty thresholds for industrial concessions.

qa_pairs.question: In 2016-06-02, Customs Agent Licensing Rules were established for submitting Bills of Export. What significant change to the role of the Bill of Export occurred eight years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-06, the Export Policy/Directives mandated the synchronization of the Bill of Export with the Export General Manifest (EGM) and formally established it as a core document for post-clearance audit processes.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024-06-06 mandate for EGM synchronization, how did the role of the Bill of Export evolve less than a year later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the AEO Guidelines expanded the Bill of Export's function to facilitate self-inspection of goods and the payment of duties and taxes for AEO-certified entities.

qa_pairs.question: Two years after the integration of TIN into factory inspection reports for concessional imports, what major directive was issued regarding the role of TIN in regulatory audits?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2023-09-27, the System-Based Audit Directive was issued, establishing the TIN as a primary identifier for system-based audit and transaction retrieval.

qa_pairs.question: One week after the Income Tax Act 2023 compliance mandate for foreign directors, what specific requirement was introduced for formal firm profile affidavits?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-13, the Corporate Profile Affidavit was introduced, which mandated the requirement of an 'updated' TIN in formal firm profile affidavits.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016, what significant structural change to the appeals process was introduced one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2017-06-01, the Amendment to Licensing Rules was introduced, which modified the appellate authority structure by allowing aggrieved customs agents to file appeals against decisions made by the licensing authority under rule 21.

qa_pairs.question: What major shift in the regulatory scope for Customs Agents occurred six years later in 2023?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023-09-27, the Risk Management Directive was introduced, which expanded the regulatory framework to include risk-based profiling for Customs Agents during customs clearance.

qa_pairs.question: What administrative requirement for document submission was formalized the following year?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-06-06, the Electronic Submission Directive was issued, which formalized the use of electronic document submission while maintaining the Commissioner's authority to require physical, signed documents.

qa_pairs.question: In 2021-08-29, traditional banking was still permitted as a fallback for customs payments. How did the regulatory landscape for these payments change nearly three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2024-06-06, the regulations introduced a strict requirement for electronic payment systems for all charges and established the introduction of pre-payment accounts for express services, removing the reliance on traditional banking as a fallback.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the pre-payment account system for express service providers introduced on 2024-06-06, what development occurred the following year?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-02-17, the authorities issued a directive that reiterated and refined the pre-payment account system requirements for express service providers, ensuring they maintain sufficient balances at designated bank branches.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial 2018-06-26 directive regarding service provider responsibilities, what significant shift in technical and contractual compliance occurred nearly six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In the 2024-03-31 directive, the scope of service provider responsibility was refined to explicitly require adherence to contractual terms for tax and fee payments, while adding specific technical mandates for maintaining, updating, and ensuring the real-time operation of e-lock devices.

qa_pairs.question: In 2013-06-06, a directive was issued regarding expert services for vessel machinery; what regulatory change regarding Authorized Economic Operators occurred 11 years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-06-13, a provision was established allowing for the suspension or cancellation of an Authorized Economic Operator's recognition certificate due to violations such as false information, smuggling, tax evasion, or misuse of concessional imports.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, the NBR initially invoked Item 21 for licensing rules; what regulatory action regarding baggage rules was taken six years later, and which specific item of the Third Schedule was cited as the basis?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, on 2016-04-08, SRO 152/2015 was issued, which invoked Item 17 of the Third Schedule to provide the legal basis for amending baggage rules.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016-04-08 baggage rule amendments, what new legal basis for rule-making was introduced two years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Two years later, on 2018-06-26, SRO 198/2018 was issued, which introduced Paragraph 8 of the Third Schedule as a specific legal basis for rule-making.

qa_pairs.question: After the introduction of Paragraph 8 in 2018-06-26, what significant administrative action regarding baggage rules occurred five years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, on 2023-06-01, SRO 133/2023 was issued, which utilized Item 17 of the Third Schedule to authorize the repeal of obsolete baggage rules.

qa_pairs.question: In the initial 2010 rules, the term 'Schedule' was defined as any schedule appended to the rules; how was this definition treated six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, in the 2016-04-08 rules, the definition remained legally static, reiterating that 'Schedule' refers to any schedule appended to the rules.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 definition of 'Schedule', what happened to this definition seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven years later, in the 2023-06-01 rules, the definition remained consistent, continuing to define 'Schedule' as any schedule specifically contained within the rules.

qa_pairs.question: Given the definition of 'Schedule' in the 2023 rules, how did this definition evolve one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, in the 2024-06-06 rules, the definition of 'Schedule' remained legally static, serving as a consistent foundational anchor within the updated 2024 context.

qa_pairs.question: In the context of the baggage declaration rules established on 2024-06-06, what regulatory change occurred one month later regarding compliance timelines?
qa_pairs.answer: One month later, on 2024-07-08 via SRO 229/2024, the authority extended specific compliance timelines within Schedule-4, substituting the previous sixty-day period with a ninety-day period for licensee conditions.

qa_pairs.question: One year after the initial broad-based exemption framework was established in 2014, what specific refinement was introduced regarding the scope of Regulatory Duty exemptions?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2015, specifically via SRO 148-Law/2015, the scope of the exemption was refined by introducing a specific threshold of 5% ad valorem.

qa_pairs.question: Nine years after the 2015 direct imposition of specific Regulatory Duty rates on industrial raw materials, what major change occurred in the legal authority governing Regulatory Duty administration?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024, the legal authority for Regulatory Duty administration transitioned from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.

qa_pairs.question: In 2015-06-04, the scope of the amendment process included the insertion of new conditions and HS code adjustments. Nine years later, what major transition occurred regarding the legal basis for these amendments?
qa_pairs.answer: Nine years later, in 2024-07-08 (SRO 227/2024), the legal basis for amendments transitioned from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial regulatory amendment mechanism established on 2010-06-10, how did the scope of the amendment process change five years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, on 2015-06-04 (SRO 138/2015), the scope of the amendment process was expanded to include the insertion of new conditions and specific HS code adjustments, beyond the simple HS code replacements used previously.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the 2011 Customs Act Amendment which defined information for whistleblowing rewards, how did the requirement for information submission regarding duty drawback evolve 10 years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2021-08-16, the Duty Drawback Regulations were introduced, which standardized information submission for duty drawback based on input-output coefficients for exporters opting for the flat-rate system.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2021 Duty Drawback Regulations, what was the primary shift in the focus of customs information and audit procedures two years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023-09-27, the Post-Clearance Audit Directive shifted the focus of customs procedures to data-driven transaction audits and mandated strict confidentiality for sensitive information.

qa_pairs.relative_offset: one year and four months later
qa_pairs.question: In the context of the 2023 Post-Clearance Audit Directive, what major institutional and procedural change regarding information-driven tools occurred one year and four months later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-01-21, the AEO Recognition Regulations were enacted, which formalized inter-agency data exchange and implemented automated risk management lanes (Red/Yellow/Green) as primary information-driven tools.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the issuance of SRO 169-AIN/2012, what regulatory adjustment occurred one year later regarding duty rates for specific exempted categories?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, in 2013-06-06, SRO 145-AIN/2013 was issued, which reduced the duty rates for specific exempted categories from 3% to 2%.

qa_pairs.question: Following the HS Code substitution established in 2012, what significant shift in exemption administration occurred nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Nine years later, on 2021-06-03, SRO 120-AIN/2021 was issued, marking a shift to alignment with the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 for the administration of exemptions.

qa_pairs.question: What major legal transition regarding the Customs Act framework took place three years after the 2021 alignment with the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, on 2024-06-06, SRO 193-AIN/2024 was issued, which transitioned the framework for local industrial exemptions to the Customs Act, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial imposition of the 5% Regulatory Duty in 2013-07-01, what change was introduced to the RD rates three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, in 2016-07-01 (SRO 223-AIN/2016), the Regulatory Duty rates were refined and adjusted to 3% for specific categories.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2014 terminology shift, what major structural change to customs financial security was introduced nearly 11 years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, a directive introduced a tiered security system, allowing partial bank guarantees (75% or 50%) combined with formal undertakings on stamp paper, moving away from the rigid requirements previously established.

qa_pairs.question: What new mechanism for consolidated customs security was introduced a few months after the January 2025 directive on tiered security?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-06-02, the 'Consolidated Guarantee' (Samanwito Guarantee) was introduced, allowing Authorized Economic Operators (AEOs) and transit/transshipment operators to use a single bank guarantee to cover multiple shipments.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the mandate established on 2023-09-27, how did the role of the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate expand in terms of operational authority by early 2025?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the Commissionerate's mandate expanded beyond audit selection to include real-time lane management, oversight of AEO status, and the authority to suspend automated benefits for entities when irregularities or tax evasion are detected.

qa_pairs.question: Following the operational directives issued on 2025-01-21, what major institutional change occurred regarding the Commissionerate's role in the Integrated Risk Management Committee?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-03-10, with the introduction of the Customs Risk Management Rules, the Commissionerate was formally established as a primary regulatory body and a core member of the centralized Integrated Risk Management Committee (IRMC).

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the baseline established in 2010, what significant change occurred in the regulatory framework five years later in terms of tax rate adjustments?
qa_pairs.answer: Five years later, in 2015, SRO 143/2015 was issued, which facilitated an adjustment of tax rates from 3% to 5% within the existing notification frameworks.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2015 framework, what major transition in the legal basis for issuing tax notifications occurred seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Seven years later, in 2022, SRO 128/2022 marked the transition to citing the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 as the legal basis for tax notification amendments.

qa_pairs.question: What primary legal authority was adopted for customs amendments two years after the 2022 transition?
qa_pairs.answer: Two years later, in 2024, SRO 227/2024 was issued, which adopted the Customs Act, 2023 as the primary legal authority for customs-related amendments.

qa_pairs.question: Given the framework established by SRO 149-Law/2018, what significant transition occurred in the legal basis for duty exemptions six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Six years later, on 2024-07-08, SRO 249-Law/2024 was issued, marking a transition from the Customs Act, 1969 and VAT Act, 1991 to the Customs Act, 2023 and the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the baseline of SRO 175-Law/2012, how did the regulatory scope change three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, on 2015-06-04, SRO 149-Law/2015 was issued, which focused on the refinement of terminology regarding the scope of import duty and regulatory duty.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the regulations set in 2024-06-06, what significant change occurred to the primary baggage weight allowance one year later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-03 (SRO 2025), the primary baggage weight allowance for passengers arriving by air or water was reduced from 65kg to 36kg.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010, the duty-free allowance for land route passengers was set at 300 USD. What change occurred six years later regarding this monetary limit?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016 (SRO 2016), the duty-free allowance for land route passengers was increased from 300 USD to 400 USD.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016 adjustment of the baggage allowance to 400 USD, what new restriction was introduced seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2023 (SRO 2023), a frequency cap was introduced, restricting the duty-free import benefit for land route passengers to a maximum of 3 times per calendar year.

qa_pairs.question: In 2012-06-07, the baggage allowance for airline crew was defined at 100 USD. How did this allowance change four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-06-02, the baggage allowance for airline crew was increased to 300 USD.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the 2016-06-02 policy which set the airline crew baggage allowance at 300 USD, what was the adjustment made nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2025-06-03, the allowance for airline crew was adjusted downward to 150 USD.

qa_pairs.question: In 2010-06-10, provisions were established for the duty-free import of medical equipment for sick or elderly passengers. Six years later, how did the regulatory framework reiterate this exemption for passengers regardless of their mode of transport?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2016-04-08, the rules explicitly granted the privilege to import medical equipment and wheelchairs free of all duties and taxes, confirming the exemption applies to all modes of transport including air, water, or land routes.

qa_pairs.question: Regarding the exemption for the baggage of deceased Bangladeshi citizens abroad as defined in 2016-04-08, what was the status of this provision nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Nine years later, in 2025-06-03, the provision remained in effect, maintaining that the personal baggage of a Bangladeshi citizen who dies abroad is fully exempt from all customs duties and taxes.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the framework established in 2010, what significant change in the legal basis for tax exemptions occurred nine years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2019-08-05, through SRO 256/2019, the legal basis transitioned from the VAT Act 1991 to the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012, while also incorporating the Income-tax Ordinance 1984.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2019 transition, what was the focus of the legislative alignment enacted five years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2024-02-29, SRO 39/2024 was issued to formalize the legislative alignment by explicitly updating references from the former VAT Act 1991 to the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 within the customs regulatory framework.

qa_pairs.question: Following the SRO 179/2010, what was the specific instrument issued one year later regarding HS Code substitution?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2011-06-09, SRO 170/2011 was issued, which continued the administrative practice of HS Code substitution under the authority of Section 19 of the Customs Act, 1969.

qa_pairs.question: What administrative change occurred one year after the issuance of SRO 126/2014?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on 2015-06-04, SRO 156/2015 was issued, serving as the next administrative step for HS Code substitution and duty regulation modifications under Section 19 of the Customs Act, 1969.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the establishment of the initial liaison group in 2018, what major procedural shift occurred in the AEO recommendation framework nearly seven years later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-01-21, the AEO Rules 2025 introduced a transition from general advisory roles to a highly formalized, multi-tiered institutional process that mandates specific, standardized reporting templates (Appendices) for all recommendations.

qa_pairs.question: Following the introduction of the standardized recommendation templates in early 2025, how was the composition of the liaison group expanded less than one month later?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2025-02-16, the scope of the liaison group was expanded to include broader representation from other government offices and agencies, in addition to the existing customs officials and private sector representatives.

qa_pairs.relative_offset: one year and three months later
qa_pairs.question: Following the 2022-06-09 Audit Directive, what significant change occurred in the audit reporting structure one year and three months later regarding the documentation of audit outcomes?
qa_pairs.answer: On 2023-09-27, the Audit Guidelines were issued, which mandated the use of 'Working Papers' for documenting audit results, decisions, and recommendations, requiring explicit identification of legal violations for each transaction.

qa_pairs.question: In 2013-06-06, certification was provided by PSI agencies for CIF value verification. What change occurred three years later regarding the authority responsible for certification?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, in 2016-06-02 (SRO 161-AIN/2016), the certification authority shifted from independent PSI agencies to specific industry associations, such as the Bangladesh Finished Leather, Leathergoods and Footwear Exporters Association or the Bangladesh Tanners Association, for specific consignments.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2016-06-02 mandate for industry association certification, what new level of certification authority was introduced four years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Four years later, in 2020-06-11 (SRO 2020), the certification requirement evolved to include government department-level certification, specifically requiring the Energy and Mineral Resources Division to certify specialized industrial equipment like CNG conversion kits.
